items.span_text: Bellicum shall use, and will cause its Subcontractors and Licensees to use, Miltenyi Products in accordance with all Applicable Laws and all requirements of Regulatory Authorities applicable to such use
items.annotator_notes: 4.3.2's own motivating sentence: item 1 of 2, the SELF-PERFORMANCE half. Bellicum's duty to use the Products lawfully itself, and its duty to bind its Subcontractors and Licensees to the same standard, are independently breachable -- Bellicum can comply itself while failing to police them, or the reverse -- and a breach of each is attributed differently, which is 4.3.2's locus-of-accountability test rather than 4.3's object-identity evidence. SPAN: byte-identical to the sibling item's, and deliberately so. The shared trailing object ('Miltenyi Products in accordance with...') sits after the interposed flow-down clause, so neither duty's MINIMAL complete span under 3.1 is any shorter than the other's -- exactly the collision 4.2's v0.36 amendment was written for, which resolves it by a content-based tie-break on action_accept_set membership (USE here, PROCURE/cause-family for the sibling) before falling through to ascending item_id. 'in accordance with all Applicable Laws and all requirements of Regulatory Authorities applicable to such use' is NOT a conditions entry: 3.8.2's removal test leaves the duty applying in identical circumstances and changes only the standard the use must meet, so it belongs to the object, which is why object_class carries it as the compliance root. object_class follows 4.3.2's v0.37 recommended self_/third_party_ prefix convention over a shared root. obligee ABSENT: no dative names a beneficiary anywhere in the span, so 3.5 forbids inferring Miltenyi from elsewhere in the document; 3.9 trigger 1 then makes underspecified true.

items.span_text: Bellicum shall use, and will cause its Subcontractors and Licensees to use, Miltenyi Products in accordance with all Applicable Laws and all requirements of Regulatory Authorities applicable to such use
items.annotator_notes: Item 2 of 2, the THIRD-PARTY-COMPLIANCE half of 4.3.2's flow-down split. obligor stays Bellicum, never the Subcontractors or Licensees: they are not bound by this obligation at all, they are the target of Bellicum's own oversight duty (4.3.2 item-2 rule, stated in terms). Modality MUST from 'will cause', read as a party undertaking under 3.2's will-rule rather than as a future fact about the agreement. ACTION IS THE WEAK POINT and is handled by 3.4's accept-set rather than by picking one verb confidently: 'cause X to do Y' has no exact match in the closed 34-verb taxonomy, which 4.3.2 acknowledges in terms ('apply 3.4's accept-set discipline rather than hard-coding one verb'). PROCURE is my single best value on the ground that 8.8 already records 'arrange'->PROCURE as a defensibly-landing mapping and procuring a third party's performance is the same shape. I did NOT tag action_not_in_taxonomy: 8.8's tag is reserved for the genuine-gap class where no member is defensible, and 4.3.2's own text treats this as an accept-set problem, not a taxonomy gap. compiler/ast.py is outside this pass's permitted directory so I could not verify which of PROCURE/ENSURE/REQUIRE/CAUSE are actually ACTIONS members; the set is authored from the sentence alone per 3.4's justification test. Span and object_class rationale as for item 1.

segment_notes: 2 items -- 4.3.2's precedent-setting sentence, split into a self-performance duty and a third-party-compliance (flow-down) duty. Counted as 2 obligation-bearing clauses, inside 2's 1-3 band. The leading '(5)' is an enumeration marker, not content; per 2.6 an incidental list marker on a sentence that carries its own subject and modal does not make the segment an orphan fragment, and this sentence is fully self-contained -- 'such use' resolves to the use named earlier in the same sentence. No 2 exclusion applies: not a definition/recital/table, not 4+ chained obligations, and 'in accordance with all Applicable Laws and all requirements of Regulatory Authorities' is a general standard rather than a cross-reference whose resolution any scored field depends on (2, v0.28 test). Both items carry byte-identical spans by necessity; 4.2's v0.36 content tie-break rather than IoU is what discriminates them.
